summary: The external-source extension accepts explicitly pinned local directories or HTTPS envelopes into a closed, bounded data population before selecting an existing catalog provider. Source-set/policy arrays are bounded before copying; manifests and ZIP inventories reject file/ancestor aliases including the fixed source.json. Cache verification rehashes the exact population, and whole-set provider collisions precede cache publication. Selected handles bind the original target, provider, ordered literal overrides, raw catalog and archive identities; None target remains inspection-only. Source provenance schema3 wraps the strict catalog schema2 record; existing ownership readers retain schema1/2/3 semantics and malformed observations remain invalid rather than absent. The existing catalog executor and independent execution policy remain authoritative. A finite acquisition/retirement attempt does not guarantee CLI exit after cleanup Unknown: original first-cause diagnostics and a bounded Unknown marker are retained, and the caller holds the original owner passively without repeated release attempts. Actual CLI qualification requires an independently selected finite external custodian; process death is never semantic cleanup. This records source design and implementation only. Full project/test, supported host, installed third-party create/build/test/offline and publication acceptance remain separate obligations.
title: External provider source acquisition and unresolved custody
